title: General Motors, Lyft Partner to Develop Driverless Taxis
main_content:
The American car-maker General Motors and Lyft Incorporated, a service, reportedly will start testing GM automobiles as driverless taxis.

The Wall Street Journal said the tests will involve GM’s electric-powered Chevrolet Bolt.

GM has reportedly invested $500 million in Lyft Inc.

GM also is planning to buy Cruise Automation Inc. for $1 billion. The California-based company has been developing self-driving car technology for two years.

It [the driverless Chevrolet Bolt] is also seen as a way for GM to compete with U.S. technology companies interested in building driverless cars.

Both Tesla Motors and Alphabet Inc. have been developing such vehicles for years. Alphabet is part of the U.S. technology company Google.
